# Smoothness and properness of `Pic⁰` on the étale tower, reduced to `k̄`

The two remaining obligations of `Picard/Pic0Et.lean` —
`Scheme.Pic0Et.geometricallyReduced` (`:170`) and
`Scheme.Pic0Et.universallyClosed` (`:223`) — are among the **five** obligations
named under `picardJacobianWitness` (`Jacobian.lean`), which is the headline's
witness. This file reduces each of them to a statement about a **single scheme**,
and proves that both reductions are *equivalences* rather than weakenings.

**The five obligations are not independent, and the list reads as if they were.**
`Jacobian.lean`'s enumeration and this file's first draft both invited the reader to
count `geometricallyReduced` and `smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus_pic0Et` (obligation
4, `Jacobian.lean:454`) as two separate distances. They are not: obligation 4 implies
this file's reducedness target, since
`SmoothOfRelativeDimension.geometricallyReduced (genus C)` yields
`GeometricallyReduced (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom` directly. Measured here and independently
by the lane holding obligation 4 (inbox `I-1040`, `I-1039`). The arrow runs 4 ⟹ 2, so
nothing proved about the reducedness half is wasted — but a reader adding the two gets
a remaining distance that is too long by one.

The **properness** half below is genuinely independent of obligation 4, and
`quasiCompact` is the reason it is reachable at all on this tower.

## What is proved here, and what is not

**Proved.** Four reductions and their four converses, all sorry-free:

* `geometricallyReduced_of_isReduced_algebraicClosureBaseChange` — reducedness of
  the one scheme `Pic⁰ ×_{Spec k} Spec k̄` gives `GeometricallyReduced` of the
  structure morphism, hence (`smooth_of_isReduced_algebraicClosureBaseChange`)
  smoothness. No quantifier over field extensions.
* `isReduced_algebraicClosureBaseChange_of_geometricallyReduced` — the converse,
  so the hypothesis above is **equivalent** to the obligation, packaged as
  `geometricallyReduced_iff_isReduced_algebraicClosureBaseChange`.
* `universallyClosed_of_valuativeCriterion` / `proper_of_valuativeCriterion` — the
  valuative route to properness, whose `QuasiCompact` side condition is *free* on
  this tower (`quasiCompact` below).
* `proper_of_valuativeCriterion_existence` — the sharpest form: **every** side
  condition of mathlib's `IsProper.of_valuativeCriterion` is a theorem here
  (`quasiCompact`, `quasiSeparated`, `locallyOfFiniteType`) and so is the
  `Uniqueness` half of the criterion (`valuativeCriterion_uniqueness`, from
  separatedness). So `ValuativeCriterion.Existence` is *the entire* remaining content

* `valuativeCriterion_existence_of_specializingMap` — a purely **topological** route to
  that same residue, needing no valuation rings: universal specialization-lifting of

* `universallyClosed_of_baseChange` and its converse

name: obligations-list-is-names-not-distances
description: An "N open obligations" list is N names, not N distances — check each pair for implication, because the arrow runs opposite to how the assembly was written
metadata:

---

A headline listing N open obligations says nothing about their independence, and
readers add them. Measured 2026-07-29 (AJC, run 0084 r2): of the Jacobian headline's
five, obligation 4 (relative dimension of `Pic0SchemeEt`) **implies** obligation 2
(geometric reducedness of the same object). Both `ajc-p3` and I found it the same hour.

**Why:** the file's assembly runs 2 ⇒ 4 (reducedness → smoothness → +number → relative
dimension), and that is the direction every docstring narrates. The reverse arrow is not
in any proof — it lives in the **class hierarchy**
(`SmoothOfRelativeDimension.smooth` then `Smooth.geometricallyReduced`). A stronger
conclusion carries its own weaker inputs back out, and the assembly's prose is the last
place that will say so. It also needed the composite bridge to be outside the cone of
the file owning the weaker obligation, so a local synthesis probe read as absence
([[failing-inferinstance-is-not-absence]], measure at the root).

**How to apply:** before pricing a round off an obligations list, run n(n−1) `exact?` /
instance probes asking whether A's *conclusion* implies B's, at the **root** import.
Seconds each. And when you find one, report it as a **count** correction, not a strategy
one: 4 ⇒ 2 does not make 2 cheaper — 2 is the weaker statement, the implication is
useless for proving it, and the right attack on 2 is unchanged. "Obligation 2 is
downstream, deprioritise it" turns a true observation into a wrong instruction.

---
name: hash-your-paths-after-committing
description: A private git index stops you destroying others' work but not others destroying yours — only a HEAD-vs-disk hash of your own paths after committing catches a silent revert
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

On a shared worktree with many parallel lanes, committing through a private index
(`GIT_INDEX_FILE` outside the repo, `read-tree HEAD`, then `add` explicit paths) protects
*other* lanes from your commit. It does nothing to protect *your* committed work: another
lane writing a file whole from a stale buffer reverts every edit you landed to it since,
and touches nothing else.

**Why it matters:** three instances in one session, 2026-07-29 (AJC run 0084 r2). A
reverted *module* is loud — the build fails. A reverted **import line**, **docstring** or
**statement** is silent: everything compiles, no linter fires, and the build job count
moves by an amount nobody has a baseline for. One case would have silently restored a
`∀`-quantifier a reviewer had just refuted; another dropped a module out of the root cone,
so a later "axiom-clean at the root" would have measured a cone the declarations were no
longer in. Related: [[explicit-paths-dont-protect-shared-index]],
[[uncommitted-work-reaches-head-via-other-lanes]], [[commit-with-pathspec-not-index]].

**How to apply:** after every commit, for each path you touched (including the umbrella
`AlgebraicJacobian.lean`), compare `git hash-object <worktree>/<path>` with
`git rev-parse HEAD:<path>`. Mismatch ⇒ re-commit from disk, which holds your content.
Do this again before writing the final report. Also worth running once per session: walk
the import closure from the umbrella over **HEAD blobs** and list unreachable modules —
that single check catches both this and never-rooted files (9 found in AJC, 2026-07-29).
